meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (root 'чистить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to teeth'.

examples.text: Для них это просто как зубы почистить!
examples.trans: For them it is simply like brushing their teeth!

examples.text: Ведь для нас это как зубы почистить!
examples.trans: After all, for us it is like brushing our teeth!

examples.text: Почему нельзя рассказать подруге, как почистила зубы?
examples.trans: Why can I not tell a friend how I brushed my teeth?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('nobody') that declines for case depending on its grammatical function in the sentence.

examples.text: Никто не придаёт этому большого значения.
examples.trans: Nobody attaches great importance to this.

examples.text: Никто не войдёт.
examples.trans: Nobody will come in.

examples.text: Я знаю город как никто.
examples.trans: I know the town like nobody else.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'great', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Никто не придаёт этому большого значения.
examples.trans: Nobody attaches great importance to this.

examples.text: Шеф, ну не расстраивайтесь вы так сильно!
examples.trans: Chef, well do not get so upset like that!

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'big', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Вчера вечером у нас случилась большая оплошность.
examples.trans: Last night a big indiscretion happened between us.

examples.text: Никто не придаёт этому большого значения.
examples.trans: Nobody attaches great importance to this.

examples.text: Тоже мне, нашёлся большой знаток современной жизни!
examples.trans: Some great expert on modern life you turned out to be!

meanings.note: Verbal action or result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание', meaning 'meaning' in conversational and formal Russian.

examples.text: Никто не придаёт этому большого значения.
examples.trans: Nobody attaches great importance to this.

examples.text: Не надо придавать этому вечеру большого значения.
examples.trans: There is no need to attach great importance to this evening.

examples.text: Это не имеет значения.
examples.trans: That does not matter.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'too'.

examples.text: Тоже мне, нашёлся большой знаток современной жизни!
examples.trans: Some great expert on modern life you turned out to be!

examples.text: Я тоже.
examples.trans: Me too.

examples.text: Он тоже здесь.
examples.trans: He's here too.

найтись.gloss: to be found, to turn up

meanings.en: to be found, to turn up
meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (root 'йтись'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to be found', forming an aspectual pair with 'находиться'.

examples.text: Тоже мне, нашёлся большой знаток современной жизни!
examples.trans: Some great expert on modern life you turned out to be!

examples.text: Скажите спасибо, что собака нашлась.
examples.trans: Say thank you that the dog was found.

examples.text: Ключи нашлись!
examples.trans: The keys turned up!

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'life', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Тоже мне, нашёлся большой знаток современной жизни!
examples.trans: Some great expert on modern life you turned out to be!

examples.text: Шеф, ну не расстраивайтесь вы так сильно!
examples.trans: Chef, well do not get so upset like that!

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'modern', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Тоже мне, нашёлся большой знаток современной жизни!
examples.trans: Some great expert on modern life you turned out to be!

examples.text: Я человек современный и всё правильно понял.
examples.trans: I am a modern man and understood everything correctly.

examples.text: Это сложная современная техника!
examples.trans: This is sophisticated modern equipment!

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'life', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Тоже мне, нашёлся большой знаток современной жизни!
examples.trans: Some great expert on modern life you turned out to be!

examples.text: Такая жизнь.
examples.trans: That's life.

examples.text: Я хочу другую жизнь.
examples.trans: I want a different life.

говорить.gloss: to speak, to say, to talk

meanings.en: to speak, to say, to talk
meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to speak', forming an aspectual pair with 'сказать'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Но вчера вечером ты говорила совсем другое!
examples.trans: But last night you were saying something completely different!

examples.text: Вчера говорил напиток, а сейчас говорит начальник!
examples.trans: Yesterday the drink was speaking, and now the boss is speaking!

examples.text: Да, вы всегда так романтично говорите!
examples.trans: Yes, you always speak so romantically!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('such') that declines for case depending on its grammatical function in the sentence.

examples.text: Ты такая смешная, когда крепко спишь.
examples.trans: You are so funny when you are fast asleep.

examples.text: Мне вообще нельзя такие тяжести таскать!
examples.trans: I must not haul such heavy loads at all!

examples.text: Не говори мне такой ерунды, Лёва!
examples.trans: Do not talk such nonsense to me, Lyova!

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'nonsense', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Прекрати сейчас же всю эту нежную ерунду!
examples.trans: Stop all this mushy nonsense right now!

examples.text: Не говори мне такой ерунды, Лёва!
examples.trans: Do not talk such nonsense to me, Lyova!

examples.text: Да ерунда, мне даже нравится.
examples.trans: That's nothing, I even like it.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to want', forming an aspectual pair with 'захотеть'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Я просто хотел вас немного успокоить, шеф.
examples.trans: I just wanted to calm you down a little, Chef.

examples.text: Витя, я хотела убедиться, что всё хорошо.
examples.trans: Vitya, I wanted to make sure that everything is fine.

examples.text: Я хочу серьёзно поговорить сегодня о нас.
examples.trans: I want to talk seriously about us today.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'a little'.

examples.text: Поработать немного надо.
examples.trans: I need to do a bit of work.

examples.text: Я немного устал.
examples.trans: I'm a bit tired.

examples.text: Мы даём вам ещё немного времени.
examples.trans: We are giving you a little more time.

успокоить.gloss: to calm down, to soothe, to reassure

meanings.en: to calm down, to soothe, to reassure
meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (root 'спокоить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to calm down', forming an aspectual pair with 'успокаивать'.

examples.text: Я просто хотел вас немного успокоить, шеф.
examples.trans: I just wanted to calm you down a little, Chef.

examples.text: Успокоить жену!
examples.trans: Calm your wife down!

examples.text: Успокоить жену! Подготовиться и поехать на дебаты.
examples.trans: Calm your wife down! Get ready and go to the debate.

meanings.note: Declinable neuter noun meaning 'matter', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Ладно, у меня много дел, я побегу!
examples.trans: All right, I have a lot to do, I will run along!

examples.text: У меня много дел.
examples.trans: I have a lot to do.

examples.text: Как дела?
examples.trans: How are things?
